extracted.intended_audience: students and aspiring literary thinkers/writers (university-level audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and prescriptive principles for becoming a serious thinker/writer: where to draw intellectual sources, habits of work and character, and how to relate to society, tradition, language and nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of intellectual sources
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ajattelijan apulähteet ovat yhtä laajat kuin luonto ja totuus" — the thinker's sources should be as wide as nature and truth; he only truly possesses them when he strives to attain them with suitable intellectual magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue the widest possible material—nature, history, and truth—while recognizing that these sources are not personal possessions but vast, impersonal reserves to be served. Treat works of past thinkers and great events as material to inform and enlarge your thinking rather than as possessions to cling to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual independence and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Jätä minut yksin; älä opeta minulle Leibniztä äläkä Schellingiä" — the thinker must cultivate original thought and not depend on merely repeating predecessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust your own thought and give yourself room to discover; avoid mechanical imitation or treating past systems as authorities. Use previous systems as data or 'ainehistona' to be absorbed and transformed by your own vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of history and exemplary lives to build confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The histories and biographies of great men increase our self-confidence by showing what humans can be and achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study lives of great thinkers and artists (Platon, Shakespeare, Milton, etc.) not as models to copy slavishly but as proofs that lofty achievement is possible and as inspiration for striving; let these exemplars encourage effort and aspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solitude as a working condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The thinker 'must embrace solitude like a bride' and be 'yksinäinen' in order to become acquainted with his thoughts and allow inward growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdraw from the desire for company and publicity when preparing serious work; practice periods of quiet and seclusion to concentrate and allow original ideas to surface. Beware of a form of solitude that is merely a prelude to immediate public exhibition—true solitude must be followed by mature expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-discipline and ascetic training
rubrics_metrics.description: Demanding training and order are necessary: rigorous self-control ('ankarampaa koulutusta ja järjestystä'), even extended periods of austere work (the tongue-in-cheek suggestion of 'five long, strict Pythagorean years').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate habits of restraint, sustained labor, frugality of distractions, and long-term commitment to craft; prefer steady, exact work over promises or idle dreams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral character and modesty
rubrics_metrics.description: The thinker should be 'yksinäinen, työteliäs, vaatimaton ja hyveellinen sielu' — solitary, industrious, modest and virtuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal virtue (humility, integrity) is integral to intellectual greatness. Avoid vanity, social posturing, and moral laxity; allow ethical seriousness to underpin intellectual practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dependence on external supports and applause
rubrics_metrics.description: One must 'hylkää kaikki vieraat tuet' and not demand anything of people; do not seek validation from crowds, parties, or revolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not build your thought or self-worth on external props (political parties, popular applause, social rank). Stand alone on the basis of your own judgment; excessive reliance on numbers and public affirmation weakens the thinker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and receptivity (expand your capacity to receive)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Älyn kasvu on vastaanottamiskyvyn laajentumista" — growth of the intellect equals expansion of receptivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate an open, receptive disposition rather than merely accumulating technical skills or doctrines. Allow immediate feeling and perception to inform thought; be willing to receive and transform impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground thinking in everyday human life and particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Work must be directed at people 'in their homes' and at the ordinary details of life rather than merely at names in books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study concrete human situations—love, work, sickness, household life, debt, honor, etc.—to provide the richest material for thought and art. Avoid writing about abstractions divorced from lived particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language should serve thought, not showmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers who 'opettelevat prameilemaan' with language and parade it are robbing language of its power; language is the 'weapon of thought and justice' and must be used for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use style and eloquence as instruments for expressing truth and moral vision, not as an end in itself. Avoid ostentatious verbal display that substitutes brilliance for substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful attention to small details and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Napoleon's success is attributed to preparation and painstaking attention to the smallest details: means toward ends, calculation and patience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not neglect minor facts or practical preparation; pair high aims with meticulous method. Treat small tasks seriously—being faithful in minutiae earns the right to larger effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance calculation with confidence in the soul's freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Napoleon combined exact calculation of means with belief in the free power of the soul; he did not neglect either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine rigorous, rational method with trust in intuition, will, and creative freedom. Neither pure cold calculation nor blind faith suffices alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw inspiration from nature's immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Latinate and English poetry have praised flowers, birds and sky, but the true thinker must go into nature where all is fresh and newly felt—'when one stands by the sea or walks in the wood one feels oneself the first person ever there.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage direct observation of nature (its tiny details, sounds, smells, and rhythms) as a source of fresh feeling and original imagery. Do not rely solely on literary conventions about nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and yielding to immediate feeling as source of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Greatness is simple; it comes when we yield excessive intellectual control and allow immediate feeling and inspiration ('todella yksinkertainen on suurta').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overrefinement and the obsession with complexity for its own sake; permit direct feeling and spontaneous expression to shape creative output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat philosophical and literary systems as raw material
rubrics_metrics.description: All systems (Plato, Bacon, Kant, eklektics) should be viewed ultimately as facts and source-matter; truth cannot be forced by mechanical comparison of systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare, study and sift systems, but do not expect them to produce truth by aggregation; allow your individual insight into facts to reorder and synthesize them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief in continual renewal of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought renews itself daily by divine power; do not bemoan age or suppose that nothing new can be said because the world is old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidence that new genuine thought is always possible; resist fatalistic claims that everything has already been said.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use both solitude and society wisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Try both solitude and companionship to see which benefits you; make use of both services but do not serve either ('Hän käyttäköön hyväkseen kumpaisenkin palvelusta, mutta älköön palvelko kumpaistakaan').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with periods of quiet seclusion and engaged social life; draw on what each offers while avoiding becoming dependent on either for identity or ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid craving public display and fame
rubrics_metrics.description: The desire for 'loistamisen ja esiintymisen halu' is fatal to the thinker; those who seek to shine as entertainers lose their private, authentic life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the lure of public notoriety, newspaper fame, and social spectacle. Prioritize integrity of inward work over public applause; fame that substitutes for genuine effort is corrosive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness in small duties as prerequisite for larger success
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept and use success only by being faithful in the smallest matters; 'oppikoon vastaanottamaan sen ja sitä käyttämään olemalla uskollinen pienimmissäkin asioissa.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate reliability and excellence in mundane responsibilities; ethical and practical trustworthiness in little things is the foundation for higher achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be receptive to spontaneous inspiration (conversational and situational)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice the 'miracle of unprepared discussion' when an otherwise modest man, stirred by an occasion, speaks freely and eloquently; permit such spontaneous impulse to emerge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the capacity to let ideas come easily in the moment: practice listening, loosen self-consciousness in appropriate contexts, and allow impromptu expression as a legitimate source of creative material.
